reason: The immediate goal is to switch the station to its planned reserve, and the charged battery at the shutdown controls seems like the direct way to do that.
expectation: I expect the station to switch to reserve power and shut down industrial loads, though the shutdown may require other actions too.

alternatives.reason: Moving the heat store into the nook could help protect the garden, but establishing reserve power seems more urgent.
The outdoor line will lose heat, so its shutdown may matter, but I would first put the station on reserve.

effect: The reserve now powers essential equipment, but normal garden circulation is off, so the crops need the protected nook and its low-power outlets.
reaction: The dimming lights and quiet fuel plant make the storm feel immediate.
reason: The outdoor line will lose heat, so shutting it down seems like a useful next step for putting the station on reserve.
expectation: I expect the water line to be isolated or otherwise protected during shutdown, though I don't know exactly what the controls will do.

alternatives.reason: Moving the heat store into the nook would help protect the garden, but the exposed water line also needs attention.

effect: The outdoor line is drained and isolated, completing the reserve shutdown; the next goal is to move both troughs into the nook.
reaction: Draining the line makes practical sense now that its heat is going away.
reason: The warm tank can help keep the nook suitable for the crops, so I’ll place it there before moving the troughs.
expectation: I expect the heat store to provide slow warmth inside the nook, though the troughs may need separate connections for circulation.

alternatives.reason: Moving the lettuce directly advances the new goal, but I want the heat source in place first.
The potato trough also needs shelter, but the heat store seems useful to both beds.

effect: The tank now buffers the nook for the first cold hours, while reserve power supplies longer-term heating.
reaction: It's satisfying to see the stored waste heat put to use during the storm.
reason: Both troughs need shelter, so I’ll move the lettuce first.
expectation: I expect the lettuce trough to move into the buffered nook; it may still need a circulation connection.

alternatives.reason: The potato trough also needs to move, and I expect to bring it in next.

effect: The lettuce is sheltered with its own reservoir, and the potato trough still needs to move.
reaction: Keeping the bed level and protecting the leaves makes the move feel practical.
reason: The potato trough is the only remaining gameplay option and must join the lettuce in the nook.
expectation: I expect the potato trough to be sheltered in the nook, completing the goal to move both troughs.

effect: The potato bed is sheltered alongside the lettuce, completing the chapter’s goals.
reaction: It was satisfying to see both beds fit while keeping their reservoirs and foliage protected.

mostWorthwhile.text: Moving the stored heat into the nook was most worthwhile: it showed how recovered waste heat could soften the first cold hours while reserve heating takes over.

leastWorthwhile.text: Moving the second trough felt somewhat repetitive after moving the first, although its deeper bed and support made the details distinct.

surprise.text: I was surprised that draining the outdoor line still left its pump and thaw checks on essential power, so the inlet can stay closed until the line is ready.

arbitrary.text: None felt arbitrary. The reserve shutdown, line drainage and sheltered beds all had clear purposes.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the station and specimens fare through the storm; the discovery and the interrupted return have made me curious.
